newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Peseta bonds ended a touch higher on Thursday after a volatile session following comments from U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that the central bank must act pre-emptively to check inflation.
"We were already scared of a U.S. rate hike on March 25. But this has made us even more scared," a Madrid dealer said.
An outperforming Italian market, boosted by positive March inflation expectations, was supporting Spanish debt, dealers said.
In the longer term, dealers said the outlook was still mildly bearish, although they ruled out any big moves on Friday.
Another issue supporting the Spanish market was a rebounding peseta, which ended around session highs against the mark at 88.88/91.
Dealers said the three-year benchmark 9.4 percent April 1999 bond recovered a bit after the previous day's heavy selling. It ended the day at 106.38 with a yield at 6.01 percent.
